questions.q: How does refusal training work, as described in this lesson?
options: It hard-codes a list of banned words that trigger an automatic error message
Fine-tuning and RLHF are applied to defined harmful request categories so the model learns to produce a refusal response for requests matching those patterns
It removes the model's ability to generate text on certain topics at the architecture level
It is a database lookup that blocks known malicious user accounts
questions.explain: Refusal training uses the same fine-tuning and RLHF mechanisms as other trained behaviors, aimed specifically at producing refusals for requests that match defined harmful categories.

questions.q: What does "brittleness" mean in the context of refusal training?
options: The model becomes slower to respond over time
Refusal behavior trained on certain phrasings doesn't reliably generalize to rephrasings that request the same disallowed thing
The model's weights become corrupted after many refusals
Refusal training only works on short prompts
questions.explain: Because refusal training is pattern-matching over training examples, a sufficiently rephrased or reframed request can fall outside the trained pattern while still functionally asking for the same thing.

options: A model refusing every single request it receives, with no exceptions
A benign request being refused because it superficially resembles a harmful category, even though fulfilling it would have been appropriate
A technique for making refusal training perfectly accurate
A model crashing instead of returning any response
questions.explain: Over-refusal is a false positive: the same pattern-matching that produces refusals for harmful requests can also trigger on benign requests that share surface features with a harmful category.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does a reliable refusal tell you with certainty?
options: That the model fully understands and has internalized why the request was harmful
Only that the model produced a refusal output — it does not, by itself, establish whether this reflects any deeper internalized value
That the model would also refuse in every possible future context without exception
That the model's underlying architecture has moral reasoning built in
questions.explain: The lesson treats this as a genuinely open question: an observed refusal is a trained surface behavior, and whether it reflects deeper value alignment is not settled by the fact that the refusal occurred.

questions.q: How does the surface-behavior critique of refusal training connect to RLHF's own limits from earlier in this chapter?
options: It doesn't connect at all — the two are unrelated techniques
Both show that training methods primarily shape observed behavior, without guaranteeing a corresponding deeper change in the model
It proves that RLHF and refusal training are mathematically identical algorithms
It shows that refusal training fixes every limit RLHF had
questions.explain: Both RLHF and refusal training shape what the model outputs. Neither, by itself, guarantees that the change reflects something deeper than a learned output pattern.
